# THE FANATIC EDITION

### 1. Meet Your Insider
Well hello, Hoosier Nation, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Mallory Penhallow, former Miss Monroe County runner-up, and these days I run a 40-tab efficiency model on everything this football team does. I travel with the team, I live with the numbers, and yes, the clicker is rhinestone. My pageant answer to every question is the same: "It's the explosives, darling." Each week I give one opponent my honorary Miss Congeniality sash. It goes to whoever I roast the hardest, and I always do it with love. When we win, you get the full pageant wave. When we lose, it's "grace in defeat"... and then I quietly open tab 41. (Fictional character.)

### 2. The School in 60 Seconds
Before Curt Cignetti showed up, Indiana had the most losses of any program in college football, 713 of them over 130-plus years [S15]. It had won three bowl games in its whole history, and the last one came in 1991 [S17]. Then 2025 happened. The Hoosiers went 16-0 and beat Miami 27-21 at Hard Rock Stadium on Jan. 19, 2026, to win their first national championship [S15]. The last team to win 16 games without a loss was Yale in 1894 [S15]. Quarterback Fernando Mendoza won the Heisman, and he scored the deciding touchdown himself on a 12-yard run on fourth-and-4 [S15][S16]. Cignetti's quote still sounds like an acceptance speech to me: "We won the national championship at Indiana University. It can be done." [S15]

### 3. The Coach and the Scheme
Cignetti was hired on Nov. 30, 2023 [S6]. Part of his rebuild came from bringing 13 transfers with him from his old school, James Madison [S17]. The 2026 numbers show what this team is. On offense, Indiana averages 36.6 points and 449.3 yards a game [S9]. It runs for 5.67 yards a carry [S4], and Josh Hoover has 18 touchdown passes with no interceptions [S5]. On defense, the Hoosiers allow 12.9 points a game, which ranks 4th in FBS [S9]. Opponents gain only 2.28 yards a carry [S4], and Indiana has 24 sacks against 10 allowed [S4]. The team has lost just three turnovers all season [S4] and gives up 30.7 penalty yards a game, 3rd-fewest in FBS [S9]. Clean football is my love language.

### 4. Players to Know
- **QB Josh Hoover:** 1,660 yards, 18 TD, 0 INT, 63.9% completions [S5][S9]. Against Ohio State he landed on his right shoulder, missed one play and came back [S13][S14]. I found no official status for Saturday as of Oct. 18 [S14].
- **RB Turbo Richard:** 643 yards on 87 carries, 6 TD [S5]. **RB Lee Beebe:** 575 yards on 107 carries, 4 TD [S5].
- **WR Charlie Becker:** 39 catches, 694 yards, 8 TD [S5], including 9 for 165 against Ohio State [S12]. **WR Nick Marsh:** 32 catches, 585 yards, 7 TD [S5].
- **Tobi Osunsanmi (sack leader):** 7 sacks, 11.5 tackles for loss [S5]. **Isaiah Jones:** a team-high 51 tackles [S5]. **Amare Ferrell:** team-high 2 INT [S5], with an interception against Ohio State [S12].

### 5. The Conference Picture
Indiana is 6-1 overall and 3-1 in the Big Ten, and 2-0 on the road [S3]. The Hoosiers dropped from No. 5 to No. 6 in the AP poll after losing 19-15 to Ohio State, which ended a 22-game winning streak and Cignetti's 19-game unbeaten run at home [S8][S12][S13]. In Cignetti's words: "We can accomplish anything we want, all of our goals, except going undefeated." [S12]

### 6. This Week: No. 6 Indiana (6-1) at Michigan (4-2)
**Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor · FOX** [S1][S9][S23]. The game is sold out, and it's Michigan's Block Cancer Game and Parents Weekend [S23].
**Last week:** Indiana lost 19-15 to Ohio State. On the last play, Marsh caught a fourth-and-4 pass but couldn't get his left foot down inbounds [S12][S11]. The defense held the Buckeyes to 313 yards, only 78 of them on the ground [S11]. Michigan beat Penn State 21-18 after true freshman Tommy Carr replaced Bryce Underwood at halftime [S10][S9].
**Our offense vs. their defense:** this is a real test. Michigan allows 256.5 yards a game, 3rd in FBS, and 89.7 rushing yards a game, 13th [S9]. Indiana has also been held under 75 rushing yards in each of its last two games [S13].
**Their offense vs. our defense:** Michigan averages 22.7 points a game (105th) and 165.7 passing yards (125th) [S9]. The Wolverines have lost 11 turnovers [S4] and are minus-3 in turnover margin, while Indiana is plus-3 [S9].
**Series:** Michigan leads 62-11 [S7]. Indiana won the last meeting, 20-15 in Bloomington in 2024 [S7], and the teams did not play in 2025 [S11].
**Availability:** Hoover's shoulder (above). I found no other official report for this game as of Oct. 18 [S14].
**What decides it:** (1) How healthy Hoover is and how well he throws. (2) Whether Indiana's run game can do anything against Michigan's front. (3) Who plays quarterback for Michigan, which Kyle Whittingham may not announce before kickoff [S10].
And yes, Gus Hartwell, Michigan's very charming insider, I'm holding the Miss Congeniality sash for you. With love.

Watching from Bloomington? Mother Bear's Pizza on East 3rd Street is a home-game tradition in our house.

Their losses came against Iowa (20-19) and at Minnesota (20-14) [S1]. Beating the defending national champions at home would be a résumé entry worth framing.

### 6. This Week: No. 6 Indiana (6-1) at Michigan (4-2)

**Last week:** Michigan trailed Penn State 3-0 at halftime, then scored 21 points in the second half and won 21-18 [S11][S10]. Indiana lost 19-15 to Ohio State. It was the Hoosiers' first loss in 23 games [S13].

Hoover hurt his right shoulder against Ohio State. He missed one play and finished the game [S13]. I found no official update as of Oct. 18 [S14].

# THE FANATIC EDITION

### 1. Meet Your Insider
Hi, Sun Devil Nation, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Skylar Vanterpool. Yes, I'm the girl by the pool in the giant maroon sunhat, and yes, I also have a master's degree in sports science, so I will talk your ear off about recovery windows and sweat rates. I travel with this team and live with this team. Fair warning: about every 90 seconds I'm going to remind you to drink some water. It's not a bit. Okay, it's a little bit a bit. ### 2. The School in 60 Seconds
Sun Devil football has a Rose Bowl ring to it. On Jan. 1, 1987, quarterback Jeff Van Raaphorst led a comeback as Arizona State beat Michigan 22-15 in Pasadena [S15]. The defense is where we need some shade and electrolytes: ASU allows 32.0 points and 373.2 yards a game, and 4.80 yards a carry [S2]. I could not find current, dated season defensive leaders, so I'm leaving them out rather than guessing.

### 5. The Conference Picture
Arizona State is 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 2-1 at home and 0-2 on the road, plus the Wembley win at a neutral site [S2][S18]. The Sun Devils are not ranked this week [S2]. The league losses were 55-19 at home to Baylor and 53-25 at Texas Tech [S18]. The top two Big 12 teams meet in the championship game [S4], and both teams in this one are 1-2, so this is a big afternoon in the desert.

### 6. This Week: Kansas State (4-2) at Arizona State (3-3)
**Saturday, Oct. 24 · 12:45 p.m. MST (3:45 p.m. ET) · Mountain America Stadium · ESPN2** [S3][S1]. It's K-State's first visit to Tempe since 1989 [S17].
**Last week:** ASU trailed Texas Tech 43-10 at halftime and lost 53-25 [S10]. Kansas State came from behind to beat Kansas 35-24, with 568 yards of offense and 359 on the ground [S6].
**Our offense vs. their defense:** K-State allows only 136.3 passing yards a game and has 13 sacks [S2]. Our pass protection gave up a season-high six sacks last week, even with center Tana Alo-Tupuola and guard Wade Helton back from missed time [S9][S10].
**Their offense vs. our defense:** the Wildcats run the ball well, at 6.23 yards a carry [S2]. Quarterback Avery Johnson has 462 rushing yards to go with 1,301 passing [S5], and running back Joe Jackson ran for 159 yards against Kansas [S6]. Our run defense allows 4.80 a carry [S2], so tackling is the whole story. Arizona Sports pointed to tackling as a problem at Texas Tech [S10].
**Series:** Arizona State leads 6-1 and won the last meeting, 24-14 in Manhattan in 2024 [S4][S5].
**Availability:** I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026. Dillingham said he would "assess all personnel" after watching the tape and has not named a starting quarterback [S8]. Johnson was shaken up against Kansas but said he only had the wind knocked out of him [S7].
**What decides it:** (1) Boley or Keene, and how quickly that quarterback gets settled. (2) Whether our front can win at the point of attack against K-State's run game. (3) Protection. Six sacks can't happen again.
And to Hattie Brandvold, K-State's insider: welcome to Tempe, sweetie! I left a cold water bottle at your seat. It's a dry heat, but your crops will still wilt.

# THE FANATIC EDITION

### 1. Meet Your Insider
Well, howdy, Wildcat family, and welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Hattie Brandvold. I have an agronomy degree, a purple denim jacket, a wheat-sheaf brooch and a field notebook with real Flint Hills dirt on it. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I explain defensive fronts the only way I know how: crop rotation. Every drive gets named after a crop. A three-and-out is a dry sorghum patch. A long, patient march is winter wheat. And a touchdown? That's a bumper harvest, and you will hear me holler it. When we win, I do the Wabash Cannonball in my chair, tidy and joyful. When we lose, I whisper my most treasured words, "You can't rush a harvest," and I plant a tiny basil seed right there on set. Sweet as prairie pie, until I hand you the one fact that ends the argument. (Fictional character.)

### 2. The School in 60 Seconds
Kansas State football is the story of the biggest turnaround in the sport. When Bill Snyder took over in 1989, the program was in the middle of a 27-game winless streak. He turned it into a national contender that went to 11 straight bowl games and had six 11-win seasons in a seven-year stretch [S20]. Snyder won two Big 12 championships, one in 2003 with Darren Sproles and one in 2012 [S12]. He went into the College Football Hall of Fame while still coaching, in December 2015 [S12]. The Wildcats play at Bill Snyder Family Stadium in Manhattan [S2], and the rivalry with Kansas is the Sunflower Showdown, played for the Governor's Cup [S6]. As of last Saturday, K-State has won that game 18 straight times, the longest active winning streak by any team in a rivalry game [S6]. Now that's a crop that keeps coming back every spring.

### 3. The Coach and the Scheme
Collin Klein was named the 36th head coach in school history on Dec. 4, 2025 [S11]. You may remember him as the quarterback: he was a 2012 Heisman Trophy finalist and won the Johnny Unitas Award that year, when K-State won the Big 12 [S11][S13]. He is the first K-State alum to be head coach since Ellis Rainsberger in 1975-77 [S11]. Before this job he coached nine years in Manhattan, including two as offensive coordinator (2022-23) that went 19-8 with a Big 12 title, then ran the offense at Texas A&M [S11]. The 2026 numbers say this offense grows on the ground. K-State runs on about 54% of its plays and gains 6.23 yards a carry, with 15 rushing touchdowns [S2]. Against Kansas he passed for 209 yards and a touchdown and ran for 132, and he became the school's all-time leader in total offensive yards [S6]. He went down after a 59-yard run and pointed to his right shoulder, but he returned and said, "I just got the wind knocked out of me." [S7]
- **RB Joe Jackson (senior):** a season-high 159 yards and a touchdown against Kansas [S6][S7].
- **WR Jaron Tibbs:** the team's leading receiver with 268 yards [S5].
- **K Luis Rodriguez:** four field goals against Kansas, from 22, 51, 28 and 34 yards, the second-most in a game in school history [S6].
- **DB Logan Bartley:** made an end-zone interception against Kansas [S6].
I could not find official season defensive leaders from a source newer than the start of October, so I'm not listing them.

### 5. The Conference Picture
K-State is 4-2 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 4-1 at home and 0-1 on the road [S2]. The Wildcats are not ranked in the AP or Coaches poll this week [S2]. The two league losses came at Cincinnati, 31-26, and at home against Houston, 35-16 [S2][S6]. The top two teams in the Big 12 meet in the championship game [S4], so a 1-2 start means every Saturday from here matters.

### 6. This Week: Kansas State (4-2) at Arizona State (3-3)
**Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:45 p.m. ET (12:45 p.m. MST) · Mountain America Stadium, Tempe · ESPN2** [S3][S1]. It's K-State's first game in Tempe since the 1989 season opener, and the Wildcats' last game in this stadium was a 31-14 bowl win over Michigan in 2013 [S17].
**Last week:** K-State trailed Kansas 17-7 in the first quarter, then won 35-24 and racked up 568 yards, 359 of them on the ground [S6]. Arizona State lost 53-25 at Texas Tech. Coach Kenny Dillingham replaced quarterback Cutter Boley with Mikey Keene at halftime, and Keene threw for 256 yards and two touchdowns [S8][S10].
**Our offense vs. their defense:** this is where my winter wheat should grow. Arizona State allows 32.0 points and 373.2 yards a game, and 4.80 yards a carry [S2]. Texas Tech gained 7.8 yards a play against the Sun Devils last week [S10].
**Their offense vs. our defense:** ASU throws for 276.7 yards a game [S2], and senior receiver Reed Harris is a big-play threat [S16][S9]. But the Sun Devils have allowed 15 sacks, including a season-high six at Texas Tech [S2][S9]. K-State has 13 sacks of its own [S2].
**Series:** Arizona State leads 6-1, and the Sun Devils won the last meeting, 24-14 in Manhattan in 2024 [S4][S5]. K-State's lone win was 34-27 on Dec. 27, 2002 [S5].
**Availability:** Johnson's shoulder scare turned out to be the wind knocked out of him [S7]. I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026. Dillingham has not named a starting quarterback for this game [S8][S9].
**What decides it:** (1) Can K-State's run game keep producing like it did against Kansas? (2) Who plays quarterback for Arizona State, Boley or Keene? (3) Can our pass rush get home against a front that gave up six sacks last week?
And to Skylar Vanterpool, Arizona State's insider: I'll bring the shade hat and the water jug, darlin'. Hydrate all you like. You still can't rush a harvest.

report.text:
### 1. Meet Your Insider

Well, howdy. Come on up the mountain. I'm Zebulon Coldiron, but you can call me Zeb, and I'm your App State insider at The Cover Window. I'm a fourth-generation Watauga County kid, and I learned to whittle and read a defense on the same front porch. My granddaddy could spot a blitz before the snap and carve a perfect duck in the same afternoon. I'm still working on the duck.

I don't hurry, and I don't holler (much). I treat every week like a hike: steady climbing, honest footing, then a view at the top. That means real numbers, plain talk, and a fair word for every visitor. If I don't know something, I'll tell you, and then I'll go find out. Some programs get a stadium. We got a mountain with a stadium on it. Come up for the game, stay for the leaves, and bring your grandma a jacket. (Fictional character.)

### 2. The School in 60 Seconds

Appalachian State is in Boone, North Carolina, and has played FBS football in the Sun Belt since 2014 [S5]. Before that, the Mountaineers were an FCS power from 1978 to 2013 [S5]. They won three straight national championships from 2005 to 2007, the first FCS team to do it since the playoffs began in 1978 [S5]. The program has won about 661 games and 22 conference championships, and its all-time winning percentage of .646 ranks 16th nationally [S5]. Armanti Edwards won the Walter Payton Award back to back, in 2008 and 2009, the first player to do so [S5].

Home is Kidd Brewer Stadium, named for the coach whose 1937 team went unbeaten and unscored upon in the regular season, outscoring opponents 206-0 [S5]. CFBD lists a capacity of 30,000 [S1]. The last five seasons: 10-4, 6-6, 9-5, 5-6 and 5-8 [S1].

### 3. The Coach and the Scheme

Dowell Loggains is in his second season. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 7, 2024 [S1]. He came to Boone from South Carolina, where he was offensive coordinator [S7]. Before that, he was an NFL offensive coordinator for the Titans, Bears, Dolphins and Jets [S7]. He played quarterback at Arkansas [S7].

The 2026 numbers show a passing offense with a punch: 267.7 passing yards per game (33rd in FBS) and 421.8 total (48th) [S3]. Scoring is 29.5 points per game [S3]. The run game averages 154.2 yards [S3] at 4.24 per carry [S1]. The defense allows 352.3 yards and 21.8 points per game (54th) [S3], and holds opponents to 3.68 yards per carry [S1]. The Mountaineers are +4 in turnover margin (22nd) [S3], and their red-zone offense scores 92% of the time (24th) [S3].

### 4. Players to Know

- **QB Malachi Singleton:** 113 of 169, 1,429 yards, 7 TD, 2 INT, 66.9% [S2][S3]. He started at Coastal and went 12 of 14 for 151 yards [S4].
- **QB Henry Hasselbeck:** the junior backup ran 21 times for 125 yards at Coastal and went 9 of 12 for 112 yards, including his first touchdown pass [S4]. Steady as a mule on a ridge.
- **RB Jaquari Lewis:** 346 yards on 70 carries, 8 TD [S3]. He scored four rushing touchdowns at Coastal [S4].
- **WR Sam Pickett III:** 26 catches, 411 yards, 4 TD [S3], including the 31-yard touchdown at Coastal [S4].
- **DL Caleb Sandstrom:** 5 sacks [S2]. **LB Colton Phares:** a team-high 38 tackles [S2].

### 5. The Conference Picture

App State is 4-2 overall and 1-1 in the Sun Belt [S1]. The Mountaineers are 2-1 at home and 2-1 on the road [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. The losses came at NC State (41-31) and at home to Old Dominion (10-3) [S1]. James Madison arrives at 7-0 and 4-0 in the league [S1]. A win Thursday would be the kind of view you climb all day to see.

### 6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

**James Madison (7-0) at App State (4-2)** · Thursday, Oct. 22, 7:00 p.m. ET · Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone · ESPNU [S3][S8] · It's also Family Weekend on campus [S10].

**Last time out.** We rallied to beat Coastal Carolina 35-32 on Oct. 16. We trailed 24-14 at halftime, then pulled ahead behind Lewis's four touchdown runs and ran out the clock [S4]. JMU beat Georgia State 49-22 on Oct. 17, with Camden Coleman throwing for 185 yards and two touchdowns and George Pettaway running for 119 yards [S3].

**App State's offense vs. JMU's defense.** The Dukes allow just 16 points per game (19th) and 114.3 rushing yards (35th) [S3], with 18 sacks [S1]. Their pass defense allows 236.4 yards per game (103rd) [S3], so Singleton and Pickett may find room through the air. Both red-zone offenses are strong [S3], so finishing drives will matter.

**JMU's offense vs. App State's defense.** This is the steepest part of the trail. JMU averages 42.9 points per game (3rd in FBS) and 223.6 rushing yards (14th) [S3]. Pettaway has 755 yards and seven touchdowns, per AP [S3]. Coleman has 13 touchdown passes and one interception [S3]. Our run defense allows 137.8 yards per game (60th) [S3]. ### 1. Meet Your Insider

Evenin', folks. Pull up a stump. I'm Lemuel Coxwell, but everybody from here to the Trinity River calls me Lem, and I'm your Sam Houston insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Walker County native and a high-school history teacher, and I collect Texas folklore the way some folks collect bottle caps. My students say I can turn a fire drill into a three-part saga. They're not wrong.

Here's how I'll tell it. I'll be patient, because seasons are long and young men grow. I'll be proud, because Huntsville is a small Texas town with a big Texas name, and our Bearkats play like they're carrying it. Most of all, I'll be honest. A good storyteller never needs to stretch the truth. Every number I give you will be real. If I don't know something, I'll say so plain, then go dig through the archives. (Fictional character.)

### 2. The School in 60 Seconds

Sam Houston State fielded its first football team in 1912 [S7]. Home is Elliott T. Bowers Stadium in Huntsville, which seats 14,000 [S7][S1]; CFBD lists it as built in 1986 [S1]. In 2021 the Bearkats left the Southland Conference for the WAC's FCS football league, and in November 2021 they accepted an invitation to join Conference USA at the FBS level starting in 2023-24 [S7].

The last five seasons tell a tale with some hills in it: 11-1 in 2021, 5-4 in 2022, 3-9 in 2023, 10-3 in 2024 and 2-10 in 2025 [S1]. That 10-3 year was the high mark of the FBS era so far [S1]. Every good story has a hard chapter before a good one.

### 3. The Coach and the Scheme

Phil Longo was named Sam Houston's 16th head coach on Dec. 18, 2024 [S7][S1], so this is his second season. Wikipedia describes him as a practitioner of the air raid offense [S8]. He was previously offensive coordinator at Wisconsin, and before that offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at North Carolina, Ole Miss and Sam Houston [S8].

The 2026 numbers match that reputation through the air but not on the ground. The Bearkats throw for 247.0 yards per game (51st in FBS) and run for 95.0 (134th) [S3], at 3.15 yards per carry [S1]. Scoring sits at 19.5 points per game (123rd) [S3]. The defense is split. - **WR Chris Reed:** 17 catches, 289 yards, 3 TD [S3], including three catches for 51 yards against WKU [S3].
- **LB Dean Ford:** a team-high 38 tackles [S2]. **LB Elijah Groves:** 2.5 sacks [S2].
- **K Sam Carpenter:** made a 42-yard field goal against WKU and a 36-yarder at Liberty [S4][S6].

### 5. The Conference Picture

Sam Houston is 1-5 overall and 0-2 in Conference USA [S1]. The Bearkats are 1-2 at home and 0-3 on the road [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. The two close losses came early, 24-21 at Troy and 23-17 to Tulsa [S1]. Since then it's been a steep climb: 49-14 at Texas Tech, 35-3 at Liberty and 16-3 to Western Kentucky [S1]. The lone win was 59-0 over Nicholls [S1]. A home win Wednesday would be the first league win of the season. In a long story, that's the chapter where the hero stands back up.

### 6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

**New Mexico State (2-4) at Sam Houston (1-5)** · Wednesday, Oct. 21, 8:00 p.m. ET · Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville · ESPN2 [S3]

**Last time out.** Western Kentucky won 16-3 in Huntsville on Oct. 14. Sam Houston was held to 177 total yards and 12 first downs [S4]. WKU is now 4-1 against Sam Houston and perfect since the Bearkats joined CUSA in 2023 [S4]. New Mexico State lost 22-3 at FIU on Oct. 7 [S3]. FIU's kicker made five field goals, and NMSU threw two interceptions [S5].

**Sam Houston's offense vs. New Mexico State's defense.** The Aggies allow 347.8 yards per game (61st) and are tougher against the run (125.5 yards, 47th) than the pass (222.3, 90th) [S3]. So Locke's arm is our best path. NMSU has 15 sacks [S1], with Gabe Peterson at 4.5 [S2], so protection matters. The Aggies rank 118th in red-zone defense, allowing scores on 92.9% of trips [S3]. Get there, and good things tend to happen.

**New Mexico State's offense vs. Sam Houston's defense.** The Aggies will want to run, and James Jones is the reason: 599 yards on 92 carries and three touchdowns [S3]. He entered the FIU game leading Conference USA at 102.0 rushing yards per game [S5]. Our run defense allows 200.3 yards a game [S3]. That's the whole ballgame in one sentence. Our pass defense, fourth in FBS [S3], should make the Aggies one-dimensional if we can slow Jones.

**Series.** New Mexico State leads 2-1. NMSU won 27-13 in 2023, Sam Houston won 31-11 in 2024, and NMSU won 37-10 on Oct. 2, 2025 [S9]. Those series details come from a search summary of the schools' pages, so I'm marking them thin.

**Availability.** No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S12]. I found no confirmed Sam Houston injury news. On the New Mexico State side, Adam Damante started at FIU after Trey Hedden started the first four games [S5]. Who starts Wednesday hasn't been confirmed.

New Mexico State brings its own debut insider, a chile-roasting storyteller from Las Cruces. Two storytellers, one ballgame. Somebody's tale gets a happy ending.

**Three questions that decide it:**
1. Can the Bearkats slow Jones and the NMSU run game [S3]?
2. Can Sam Houston's offense get into the red zone against a defense that rarely stops anyone there [S3]?
3. Can the Bearkats keep winning the turnover battle (+1) against an NMSU team at -5 [S3]?

### 7. Local Flavor

I'll tell you about my Huntsville haunts once I've confirmed them. Bring a lawn chair and a story. Not an ad.
